newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 24.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The United States aims at creating a bizonal, bicommunal state in Cyprus, the US presidential emissary on the divided island Richard Holbrooke said yesterday. Holbrooke, the architect of the Bosnian peace agreement, said that the Cyprus issue would be distinct from other Greek-Turkish issues.

--The national economy and finance ministry is planning a European-wide meeting on economic policies for Athens later this month with the participation of economic ministers from socialist governments as well as former European Commission president Jacques Delors.
--Final-year students around the country begin taking their university entrance examinations today.
--Greece will spend one billion drachmas on contemporary Israeli-manufactured patrol boats to combat border smuggling and other crime from Albania and Turkey. TA NEA
--Fines for tax evasion will be lower in an attempt to recoup more revenue for the state, in line with a new bill submitted to Parliament yesterday by Deputy Finance Minister George Drys.

--Forty-seven-year-old construction worker Tryfon Romiopoulos is seeking answers to why his 20-year-old soldier son was found to have died of natural causes despite two coroners disputing the findings and saying he was strangled.

--Olympic Aviation, Olympic Airways domestic flights subsidiary, has resolved its industrial conflict with technicians but the backlog of delays and cancelled flights will take until the weekend to clear.
--Yiannis Spraos, the head of the committee which drafted a report on the government's economic policy, says achieving targets will require consensus and political will.
--The government is ready to offer incentives of one trillion drachmas to shipping companies to renew their fleets at Greek shipyards. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
